tweet.text:
Ive been using Gherkin as the primary behavioral specification tool.  It works well.

I have claude or codex build a gherkin parser that generates tests.  In java they would run in junit.  The Gherkin must remain in natural language, no code level artifacts.  The parser needs to translate the Gherkin into tests that access the application directly.

It helps to build a testing api that separates the application code from the tests.  This api can be constructed once you have enough tests to see the seams.

I also have the AI follow the three laws of TDD.  They write unit level tests that fail, and then make them pass, in a very short loop.  

This gives me acceptance tests that are not code, and unit tests that are.  I've found this to be very effective.
